methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Loombotic is a robotics and manufacturing company at an undisclosed stage, founded by Lucas Crupi and Ethan Breit. The valuation universe comprises ten peers in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms. Top private comparables include Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

Peer-median triangulation was not applicable in this case. The sector contains sufficient comparable companies, but filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints in each category. A methodologically sound peer-median analysis requires a minimum of three narrowly filtered comparables to avoid distortion from stage and scale heterogeneity. Broadening to an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise, as stage-dependent valuation multiples in robotics vary significantly.

Without adequate narrow-peer density, this analysis cannot support a triangulated valuation range at present. The primary constraint is stage ambiguity: without confirmed development or funding stage information, filtering comparable companies introduces circular logic. Meaningful valuation work on Loombotic would require either clarification of its development stage and recent funding activity, or acceptance of a wider peer set with explicit stage-discount methodology. The public comparable and eight private peers remain available as reference points but do not yet constitute a defensible valuation basis.
